title: 1957 AHSME Problem 35
statement: Side \(\overline{AC}\) of right triangle \(ABC\) is divided into \(8\) equal parts. Seven line segments parallel to \(\overline{BC}\) are drawn to \(\overline{AB}\) from the points of division. If \(BC=10,\) then the sum of the lengths of the seven line segments:

answerChoices.label: A
answerChoices.text: cannot be found from the given information

solutions.text:
By similarity, the segment at the \(k\)th division point has length \(\frac{10k}{8}\) for \(k=1,\ldots,7.\) Their sum is \[ \begin{aligned} \frac{10}{8}(1+2+\cdots+7) &=\frac{10}{8}\cdot28\\ &=35. \end{aligned} \]

Therefore, the correct answer is D.
hints: Each small triangle with vertex \(A\) is similar to triangle \(ABC\)
